[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Recent Actions** [CF 1799A · Recent Actions](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1799/A){rating="800"}

Every arriving post has id $> n$, so new posts always sit *above* the surviving initial posts, and the bottom of the field is always the highest-numbered initial post still present. An action evicts someone only when its post is not yet in the field, that is, on the **first** appearance of that id (while initial posts remain, no new post is ever pushed out). So the $k$-th distinct id to arrive evicts initial post $n - k + 1$, at the time it first arrives. Record the first-arrival times (`firsts`); post $i$ is evicted at `firsts[n - i]` if at least $n - i + 1$ distinct ids arrived, else never. The timestamps answer the question without simulating the field.

[Solved in full in @sec-ds-p5-recent.]{.card-link}
